stories.title: NATO military activities in Arctic may lead to catastrophic consequences — Lavrov
stories.summary: MOSCOW, August 31. NATO’s military activities in the Extreme North raise risks of incidents with catastrophic consequences, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said in his article, ‘International Cooperation in the Arctic: Challenges and Opportunities,’ published on the arctic.ru portal. "How else can one explain the fact that NATO countries, as well as the Alliance as a whole, are driving the region towards militarisation and creating hotbeds of international tension there?" Lavrov asked rhetorically. In his words, NATO launched Operation Arctic Sentry in February 2026, aimed at expanding its military presence in the High North. "Intensive military preparations are underway in close proximity to our northern borders. NATO is conducting large-scale military exercises involving non-regional countries and introducing new components of its command-and-control system," the top Russian diplomat wrote. "Such military activity in the Far North poses a direct threat to Russia’s security. It also increases the risk of incidents that could trigger an armed confrontation with potentially disastrous consequences."

stories.headline: At least 20 missing, dozens evacuated from Grand Canyon after flash flood hits creek

opening: More than 20 people may be missing after a major flash flood at the Grand Canyon, the US National Park Service said on Sunday.
The flood forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept large boulders, metal structures and other debris into the Colorado River that runs through it, the park service said.
body: The flooding in Bright Angel Creek, which flows into the river, happened on Saturday afternoon.
Torrents of water wiped out footbridges over the creek and significantly altered the landscape,...
More than 20 people are thought to be missing or unaccounted for after flash flooding swept through parts of the Grand Canyon.
It hit at around 14:30 local time (22:30 BST) on Saturday in Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch area, according to the National Park Service (NPS).
The NPS said flooding had caused significant damage in some areas and that trails in the area have been closed.

It warned that more thunderstorms and heavy rainfall were forecast for Sunday and Monday, which could lead to "additional flash flooding, debris flows, rockfall and changing trail and river conditions".
The Phantom Ranch area can only be reached by foot, mule or by rafting the Colorado River, according to Grand Canyon National Park Lodges.

bullets.label: Next
bullets.text: Sixty-two people have so far been airlifted out of the area, with more expected to follow.
